newsitem.title: FRANCE: NATO, Russia begin summit to sign "Founding Act".
newsitem.headline: NATO, Russia begin summit to sign "Founding Act".

text.p: Leaders of the NATO alliance and Russia opened a summit meeting on Tuesday to sign a "Founding Act" laying the foundations for a post-Cold War partnership for security in Europe.

U.S. President Bill Clinton, Russian President Boris Yeltsin and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana were present as French President Jacques Chirac opened the glittering signing ceremony in the Elysee presidential palace.

The agreement, designed to overcome Russian opposition to plans to expand NATO into eastern Europe, gives Moscow a voice, but not a veto, in European security arrangements through a joint council with the 16-nation Atlantic alliance.

Yeltsin has won assurances that the allies have no plans to place nuclear weapons or foreign troops on the soil of new, former communist member states, who will be invited to join NATO at a summit in Madrid in July.

After talks with Chirac just before the summit, Clinton rejected concern in the U.S. Congress that the accord would give Moscow a veto over alliance decisions, saying: "NATO will come out of it unimpaired and with a good partner in Russia. That's what we want."

In his inaugural speech, Chirac told the leaders in the ornate Salle des Fetes banqueting room: "Today we are building peace. For the first time, the leaders of the Atlantic alliance countries and Russia are gathered together as bearers of a great ambition: to guarantee peace in Europe based on our common values and the awareness that we share the same destiny."
